sps_amber_ghosts.description:
I'm Millwright Haskell. When you get to Ambermill, watch the doorway, and don't go through it yet. There's a ward on it, and I'd rather you found out about it from a distance.

Ambermill was a Dalaran village, lumber mostly. We cut and they bought, and they kept a handful of mages there to keep the saws turning and the wards fresh.

The plague took the mages. Their ghosts stayed, and so did everything they'd set, and now I can't tell you which of them is guarding the mill and which is guarding itself. Some of them turn you back politely. Some of them don't.

Thin them out, the ghost-mages and the wardens both. I've got a mill under all this, and I'd like to get to it before the roof decides the matter.
sps_amber_ghosts.accept_text: Break the wardens first. The ghost-mages go quiet without someone keeping their wards fresh.
sps_amber_ghosts.turn_in_text:
I got into the saw-room for the first time in years.

The blades are seized but the shaft turns, which means the water's still doing its job under there. That's a mill. That's nearly a mill.

sps_amber_resin.description:
The wardens aren't ghosts, whatever anyone tells you. They're made of resin.

It's amber resin out of the lumber, hardened with magic until it holds a shape and walks about. The mages made them so there'd be something minding the yard at night, which is perfectly sensible and very Dalaran.

When they go down they leave lumps of it, and amber resin burns long and hot and clean. I want it for the stove.

He stops for a moment.

I should be straight with you, since you've done the work. There isn't a stove. There isn't a house for a stove to be in. I've been collecting fuel for two years for a hearth in a building that burned, and I know exactly what that is, and I'm going to keep doing it until I've got enough.
sps_amber_resin.turn_in_text:
He stacks them with the rest, in a neat square, under a tarpaulin.

That's nearly a winter's worth.

I'll build the house when the mill turns. That's the order I've decided it goes in, and people who argue with me about it end up not being spoken to.

sps_amber_waygate.description:
I'm Magister Orsolo. For forty years I studied the Ambermill waygate, and I'll tell you my conclusion, which is that I've stopped wanting to know where it goes.

I haven't given up. It's the most considered opinion of my career.

It leads somewhere. It has always led somewhere, and my four decades of work were all about establishing where. Then the world moved, three years ago, and a great many fixed things stopped being fixed. I went to the gate one morning, looked at it, and understood that the answer had changed and that I didn't want the new one.

So you go. Stand at it and describe it to me, only describe it. Don't speculate, and don't touch it.
sps_amber_waygate.accept_text: Go to the waygate below the tower, south-east of the mill. Describe it to me, and don't speculate or touch it.
sps_amber_waygate.turn_in_text:
Orsolo listens with his eyes shut and doesn't interrupt.

Thank you. That's exactly what I didn't want to hear, and precisely why I needed to hear it.

It's still open. It's open wider. And in forty years of measuring that thing I never once recorded it changing on its own.

sps_ashes_south.accept_text: Keep the phial in your hand, not your pack. It stays warm, and I want to know if it cools on the way.

sps_berard.description:
And then there's the man the hill's named for.

All anyone has is the name, Berard, on the hill. I've asked at Ambermill, I've asked the March, and I've had a Forsaken clerk go through what's left of the keep rolls as a favour, and his face isn't in any record anywhere. There's just the Talon, named for a man nobody can describe.

He walks the ridge every night, on the same route as the wraiths but not with them. They give way to him. And he's looking for something. You can see it in how he moves. He isn't patrolling, he's searching, and he's been searching that ridge every night for longer than there's been a record of him.

Nobody knows what for, and nobody's left who could. Let him stop looking.
sps_berard.turn_in_text:
Hask is quiet a while.

So that's the hill done, and we still don't know what he was after.

I'll keep the tokens going back regardless. It could be one of them was his, and he'll never know we found it. That's the sort of thought a man has on a hill in winter.

sps_bloated_one.description:
I've found the source. It's been in the middle of my pond the whole time, and I walked past it every day for two years thinking it was a sunken log.

There's a corpse at the heart of the water so swollen it can't rise any more. It just lies there and lashes at whatever comes near, and everything that bursts off it goes into the water and comes out of the water as something else.

That's the gas, that's the oozes, that's the whole business.

It'll burst when you hit it. I want you going in knowing that, because whatever bursts out will be worse than what was lying there. Finish it anyway. Olivia's Pond is just west of here.
sps_bloated_one.accept_text: Stand upwind when it goes. Whatever bursts out, you don't want to breathe it.
sps_bloated_one.turn_in_text:
Thorne is standing further out than you've ever seen him stand.

The water's clearing, slowly, but clearing.

It'll still be draining, mind. That space under the pond is still down there and still filling, and one day somebody will have to care about that. Today I've got my pond back.

sps_bloodmaw.description:
Bloodmaw is the reason the Peril holds.

He's grey-muzzled, old, and he's outlived every single challenger, and in a pack that advertises its rank in teeth you can read exactly how many on the collar he wears. He's got a scar the length of his flank that somebody earned and didn't survive collecting.

I want you to understand what he actually is, because alpha makes it sound like he's just the biggest. He isn't the biggest any more. He's the one who taught them the line, and the packmasters are his. Every one of those strings you brought me came off a wolf he trained.

Take him, and the Peril stops being a succession and goes back to being wolves. Beren's Peril is south of here.
sps_bloodmaw.accept_text: Watch the old scar on his flank. He favours that side, and it's the side he'll never turn to you.
sps_bloodmaw.turn_in_text:
Rynn examines the collar for a long time before she says anything.

They're scattering, and they aren't regrouping under a new one, which is what should have happened years ago.

I'll send the collar up with the rest. And then I'd like the title retired, if it's all the same. There's nothing left up there to break.

sps_dallow_reckoning.description:
Come in, and shut the door. I want to read you something.

There are five reports on this table. The Deathguard Captain is down. The Bloated One is down. Godfrey's remnant is down. Berard is at rest. Bloodmaw's pack has scattered.

That's five in a row. The March hasn't had five in a row since the war, and I include the war.

And here's what I keep turning over. Every one of those came from somebody small: a pond warden, a hearthwarden, a trapper on a hill nobody's heard of, a packbreaker with an invented title. None of them had the authority to ask for what they asked for. Every one of them asked anyway, and somebody did it.

I've written that up and sent it to the Undercity. They'll file it, but it's written down.
sps_dallow_reckoning.turn_in_text:
That's the March's thanks, for whatever a sergeant's thanks is worth.

The south road's open, the pond's clear, Pyrewood's quiet and the Peril's scattered. I came to this command expecting to lose Silverpine slowly.

Go and get something to eat. You look like a man who's been holding four conversations a day for a month.

sps_deathguard_captain.description:
There's one out on that field who was here before I was, and he's the reason the March can't hold Valgan's.

He's a Deathguard Captain, and he's still fighting the Third War. I mean that literally. He's fighting it, out there, to the original orders, against an enemy that stopped existing before I was posted to this command.

I've sent men to talk to him. I've sent a cleric. I've stood in front of him personally and used my rank, which was the most humiliating ten minutes of my career, because rank is exactly what he's still listening to, and I'm not in his chain of command, and he knew it instantly.

He won't stop and he can't be moved, and the field is his while he walks it. Put him down. He's earned better, and there isn't any better on offer.
sps_deathguard_captain.accept_text: If he gives you an order before the end, follow it. It might be the last thing he needs.
sps_deathguard_captain.turn_in_text:
Dallow is quiet a long time.

That man held this ground when holding it meant something, and he never got the order to stop.

I'm going to write that down and send it up, and some clerk in the Undercity is going to file it, and that's the whole of what any of us get.

sps_deserter_letter.description:
It's a letter taken from a dead deserter's coat, folded twice and gone soft at the creases from being carried a long time.

It's addressed to someone in the Undercity. The hand is careful, the writing of somebody who wasn't confident of their letters and took their time over every one.

The seal hasn't been broken. Whoever wrote it never sent it, and whoever carried it never opened it, and it's been going up and down a field in a dead man's pocket for months, waiting for a post that was never coming.

Someone in the March ought to read it before it goes any further.
sps_deserter_letter.turn_in_text:
Dallow breaks the seal with his thumb, reads, and puts it down carefully.

It's to his sister. He's telling her he's coming home, and asking her not to tell anyone until he's there.

That's the whole letter. There's no politics in it, no complaint about the March. He just wanted to go home, and he knew enough to know he couldn't say so out loud.

I'll post it. I'll post it, and I won't put deserter anywhere on the outside of it.

sps_deserter_tags.accept_text: Keep the tags on a cord in the order you take them. I'd like to read them out the same way.

sps_deserters.description:
Now something I'd rather not be asking a stranger to do.

Some of the March walked off. It wasn't a rout or a panic. They simply stopped, and left, and went up to the Bucklebree farm and set themselves up as brigands on it.

They did it under my nose. I'd like that on the record. I've been round it a hundred times and I can't find the morning where I'd have done differently, and it still happened on my watch and in my sight.

They're robbing carters on my road now, which makes them my problem twice over. Deal with them. I'm not asking you to do anything I wouldn't. I'm asking because a sergeant going up there personally becomes a story, and this is bad enough without being a story.
sps_deserters.accept_text: If any of them asks to come back, tell them to come and ask me. I'd rather hear it myself.
sps_deserters.turn_in_text:
Right, it's done.

I won't pretend that's a victory. Those were my people, and the fact that they stopped being my people is a thing that happened to this command. Nobody did it to us from outside.

Thank you for doing it cleanly.

sps_fenris_crossing.description:
Right, with him off the water, I can run a boat again.

I've told the March I'll take passengers to Fenris Isle. It's the first time in years anyone's said that out loud on this lake.

But I'll go as far as the pier head and not one foot past it, and I want that understood before anyone books. Whatever's on that island is the island's business.

Go and check the moorings for me. The Fenris side hasn't had a boat tied to it in a long while, and I'd rather find out the rings have rusted out of the stone from you than from a rope going slack with a load on it.
sps_fenris_crossing.accept_text: Pull on each ring with your whole weight. If it holds you, it'll hold a boat.
sps_fenris_crossing.turn_in_text:
Two rings are sound and one's gone. That's enough to work with.

I'll run the crossing from next week. Tell them at the Rear Guard. They've been asking after a way over there for a year, and I've been telling them no.

sps_ferry_crates.description:
I'm Pim, the dockhand. Mind where you put your feet. Half these boards are new, and the other half are a matter of opinion.

Cargo keeps washing up, crates, at all hours, off a boat that went down a long time ago, and the deckhands guard them. They properly guard them, stand over them, and won't let anything near.

That tells you the cargo mattered to somebody once, and I'd quite like to know who.

Get me some crates and I'll have them sent up to the Rear Guard rather than opened on this pier. If it's grain, fine. If it's gold, then the Dark Lady should have it, and I should be seen to have said so loudly and in front of witnesses.
sps_ferry_crates.accept_text: Don't open any of them on the way back, however tempting. I want witnesses.
sps_ferry_crates.turn_in_text:
They're going straight up the road, unopened, with my name on the manifest.

She gives a shrug.

I'd love to tell you I'm honest. I'm a dockhand on a lake with one road out. Being honest in front of enough people is just the cheaper way of being safe.

sps_ferry_deckhands.description:
My name's Gael, and I'm the ferryman, the current one, which is a title with more history in it than I'd like.

The crew drowned when the boat went down, all of them, in one night, and they walked back up the lake bed the next morning and went straight to the pier.

They work it. That's what I can't make anyone understand. From dusk to dawn they load cargo that isn't there off a boat that isn't there, and they're good at it, and they were good at it when they were breathing.

I sleep in the hut at the end of that pier, and I haven't slept properly in a year. Send them back, and mind the carrion birds. They've learned the crew's hours, and they come in with them.
sps_ferry_deckhands.accept_text: Go at dusk, when they start the shift. They're slowest when they're just getting up.
sps_ferry_deckhands.turn_in_text:
I slept the whole night.

I'd got so used to the sound of them working that the quiet woke me twice. Isn't that a thing?

sps_ferry_ticket.description:
It's a ticket stub for the Decrepit Ferry, soft with water and gone brown at the edges.

The stamp is still readable, dated the last winter before the plague.

The destination is Fenris Isle, and nobody has taken passengers to Fenris Isle in years, since well before the boat went down. Whoever bought this bought it for a crossing they may never have made.

The ferryman at the pier has been on this lake long enough to remember who was travelling that winter.
sps_ferry_ticket.turn_in_text:
Gael holds it up to the light.

That's the old man's stamp, my predecessor's, the one at the bottom of this lake.

The last winter before the plague. He'd have sold maybe a dozen Fenris crossings that whole season, and he knew every one of them by name.

He hands it back.

Keep it, and if you ever do get over to the isle, somebody over there may know whose it was. I'd like it to arrive.

sps_ferryman.description:
Now the one at the bottom of the lake.

The first ferryman drowned with the boat, and he came up for it. He didn't come up for us, he came up for the boat, and he's been steering it at night ever since.

I've seen it from the hut. There's a shape out there on the water at the right hour, going the right line, and there are passengers standing on it, and they aren't the sort who pay.

He taught me this crossing. Every stone and every wind on this lake I had off him, and he was a hard old man about it, and a fair one.

I'd like him in his grave rather than on my water. And I'd like to be the one who asked for it, rather than letting the March do it to him eventually without knowing who he was.
sps_ferryman.accept_text: Call his name when you see the boat. If he turns his head, he still knows who he was.
sps_ferryman.turn_in_text:
Gael is on the pier head with a lamp when you get back.

The lake's empty.

I'll take the crossing myself now, properly, in daylight, with people who pay. That's what he'd have wanted, and he'd have been unbearable about saying so.

sps_forsaken_march.description:
I'm Sergeant Dallow. This is the March, and the March exists for one reason: the road to Ambermill stays open.

That's the whole mission. Everything else we do here is in service of a supply train getting through, and at the moment a supply train wouldn't get through.

The wolves have the verge, diseased, half of them falling apart, and absolutely undeterred by that. The bears died of something the Apothecaries still haven't named, and then got up again, and now the road is lined with the leavings of both.

Thin them before the next train. I'd rather lose a day of your time than a cart of someone else's.
sps_forsaken_march.accept_text: Drag the bodies off the road when you're done. Carters won't drive past them.
sps_forsaken_march.turn_in_text:
The train came through clean this morning. It didn't even slow at the bend.

That's the job. Nobody writes songs about a cart arriving on time, and nobody should.

sps_gnawbone.description:
And then there's Gnawbone.

He was the kobold foreman before the collapse. We had kobolds on the lower drifts, everyone did, it was perfectly ordinary. He was good, and I'll say that out loud. He kept his crew working and his counts honest, which is more than I could say for two of my human gangers.

He's the only one who kept his job. He's down there now in the company hard-hat, giving orders, and the half of it I can make out is right: rotations, shoring, the order you work a face in. He learned it off me.

That's the whole trouble. He's running my mine properly and it isn't his, and I can't have both of those be true.
sps_gnawbone.accept_text: If he's still wearing the hard-hat when it's done, bring it back. That's company property too.
sps_gnawbone.turn_in_text:
Hobart turns the hard-hat over in his hands.

He kept honest counts. I want that said by somebody.

I'll put it back in the lamp room with the rest. It's company property and he was company, whatever anybody upstairs thinks about that.

sps_godfrey.description:
Then I know who it is. I've known since you said orders, and I'd been avoiding knowing for two years.

It's Lord Godfrey. He held this village, properly, in the old way, and this place ran on his say-so down to which fields got cut first.

What's in that hall is what he left behind, a ghost in a good coat with a pistol in one hand and a cane in the other, still giving the orders he was giving the night it all went wrong.

Here's what I want you to understand before you go up those steps. The dead of Pyrewood still obey him. That's why the worgen hunt like this village hunted, and why the cult found a hall with a bar on the inside. He's a chain of command, more than a haunting. Go and break it.
sps_godfrey.accept_text: Don't let him give you an order. Everyone in this village who took one is still out there.
sps_godfrey.turn_in_text:
Brand stands in the lane looking up at the hall for a long moment.

The worgen scattered, all at once, about an hour ago. There was no fight in them, they just went.

Two years I've been treating this village as four problems. It was one man with four sets of orders out.

sps_gorra.description:
There's one more, and she isn't in the pens.

Gorra is the old sow, the biggest hog in Silverpine before any of this, and I say that as a man who's been to the Ambermill fairs and seen what they bring.

She didn't die with the others. She didn't go wrong with them either, not at first. She grew instead. She's been growing for two years, and she's out past the top field now, the size of a cart. She remembers this yard, and she comes back to it at night and stands where the trough was.

He produces a knife and looks at it.

I've had this out three times. Three times I've got as far as the top field. She raised more litters on this farm than I raised children. Do it for me.
sps_gorra.accept_text: She'll charge the moment she sees you, so stand by a tree. She's never been able to turn quick.
sps_gorra.turn_in_text:
Bucklebree takes the knife back without a word and puts it in the drawer.

That's the farm finished, then, hogs, sow and all.

I'll stay on. Somebody ought to be here when the March comes through, and I've nowhere to be that isn't this.

sps_hogs.description:
My name's Bucklebree. That's my farm, and that noise is my herd, and I'd ask you not to go near the fence.

The hogs went wrong the same week the plague came through. It was the same week, not after, not gradually. They were a herd, and then overnight they were whatever that is.

They still root. That's what I can't get past. Rooting's what a hog does, and mine still do it, all day, up and down the same ground. It's just that what comes up now isn't turnips.

And they're breeding. That's the part that turns this from a sad thing into a thing somebody has to do something about. Put the herd down before there's a second generation of them in Silverpine.
sps_hogs.turn_in_text:
It's quiet now.

Forty years of pigs. I'd have told you I'd be glad to see the back of them on any given day, and I'd have been lying every time.

sps_hunter_pelts.description:
I want pelts, and clean ones.

Before you shrug and go, listen, because the difference matters, and I won't take a bag of ruined work. Diseased is fine. Half the wolves in Silverpine are diseased, and the fur comes off a diseased wolf perfectly well. Dissolving isn't fine. You'll know the difference the moment you put a knife in.

I'm making a cloak.

He waits to see whether you'll ask.

No, it's for somebody I used to know. That's the whole of the answer, and you can take it, or you can go and be useful somewhere else.
sps_hunter_pelts.accept_text: Skin them while they're fresh. A day in the sun and the rot gets into the hide.
sps_hunter_pelts.turn_in_text:
He goes through every one, feeling the backing.

These'll do, and more than do.

She was my daughter. She's buried at Ambermill, and she was cold her whole life, even in summer. She used to complain about it, and I used to tell her to put something on.

That's the answer. Don't make me give it twice.

sps_hunter_roost.description:
Here's the second thing, and this one's pure temper, so I won't dress it up as strategy.

The carrion birds follow my trap line. They've worked out the route, they genuinely have. They sit ahead of me now, and they take the kills before I've walked it.

I don't mind sharing. I'm not sentimental about a wolf carcass, and there's more wolf in Silverpine than hunters to go round.

What I mind is that they've started taking the traps. They lift them, carry them, and drop them somewhere else for no reason I can establish. I've lost a season's worth of good traps to birds that can't eat them and don't need them. Clear them off my line.
sps_hunter_roost.accept_text: Go east along my trap line, toward the Decrepit Ferry. They sit ahead of me and take the kills, and the traps.
sps_hunter_roost.turn_in_text:
I walked the whole line this morning, and every trap was where I left it.

It's a small thing, but it's been the most aggravating small thing in my life for a season.

sps_mine_gallery.description:
There's one thing in this mine I haven't looked at, and I'd like it looked at by somebody who didn't know it before.

The main gallery came down the day the plague reached us. I was on the surface. Everybody who wasn't is still in it.

I haven't been back to the mouth of it, not once in all the years since. I've had every reason and every opportunity, and I've found something else to do each time.

Stand at it and look at the supports, the big timbers at the mouth. That's all I'm asking about. Tell me whether they held.

I need to know whether it came down because the world was ending or because I signed off on those timbers.
sps_mine_gallery.accept_text: Tell me straight, whatever you find. I've waited long enough to hear it.
sps_mine_gallery.turn_in_text:
He listens very carefully, and makes you describe the timbers twice.

They held, all of them. The roof went, and the timbers held.

He sits down on an ore box.

I've carried that for years. I'd got so used to the weight of it I'd stopped noticing I was carrying anything.

sps_mine_kobolds.description:
I'm Overseer Hobart. Mind the lintel. It's lower than it looks, and it's dropped since it was cut.

I held the Deep Elem through the plague. I held it through the Scourge, and through the second strike, when half the gallery came down and we dug out from the inside.

Then the kobolds moved in, after all that. They've got the main gallery and the diggings, and they've made it theirs, properly theirs, candles and all, the way kobolds do. Every day they stay is another day this mine is a kobold warren with my name over the door.

Clear the gallery. And I want the kobolds out first, before the diggers, because I want this to be a mine with a problem rather than a warren we're visiting.
sps_mine_kobolds.accept_text: Blow out their candles as you go. A kobold in the dark is a kobold who wants to leave.
sps_mine_kobolds.turn_in_text:
I walked to the second junction with a lamp, and nothing moved.

Plague, Scourge, a collapse and kobolds. This mine has outlasted every single one, and so have I, and I intend to be extremely tiresome about that for the rest of the season.

sps_mine_lamps.description:
The shamblers in the galleries are our own. I'll say that plainly rather than have you work it out halfway down.

Deep Elem men, every one, still walking the drifts they died in and still carrying the lamps they died holding. They don't drop them. Whatever's left in a man after all that, the habit of not dropping your lamp underground outlasts it.

I want the lamps back.

He pauses for a moment. They belonged to the company. They're company property and they go in the lamp room at the end of a shift, and that's the rule, and that's why.

And because a man ought not to be carrying a lamp round a mine forever with nobody to light the way for. But put the first reason in the ledger.
sps_mine_lamps.accept_text: Take the lamps gently. A lamp pulled out of a man's hand is still a lamp he's holding.
sps_mine_lamps.turn_in_text:
Hobart hangs each one on its own numbered hook without being told which.

That's the shift in.

Thirty-one years I called that at the end of a day. I'd not expected to call it again.

sps_peril_pack.description:
I'm Packbreaker Rynn. That's a title the March invented for me, and I've decided to be proud of it.

There's a worgen pack dug in under the hills of Beren's Peril, and they aren't a pack the way the Pyrewood ones are a pack. These have packmasters, and the packmasters hold a line, an actual line, with flanks, that reforms when you break it.

I've broken a good many worgen in Silverpine. I've never had one hold a line on me.

The stalkers run out in front and screen them. Take the screen, then the line. And don't give them time to reform between, because they will, and that's the part that's been costing me people.
sps_peril_pack.accept_text: Keep moving when you break the line. Standing still gives them the time they need.
sps_peril_pack.turn_in_text:
It broke and stayed broken. That's the difference.

I've been fighting that line for a season, and losing it back every time I went for a drink.

sps_peril_teeth.description:
There's something I want, and I'll be honest that the wanting is personal.

A packmaster wears the teeth of every rival he's bested, strung at the throat, and the longer the string the longer he's held. They display it. It's a rank, more than a trophy. You can read a packmaster's whole career off his collar at twenty paces.

I want the necklaces, the strings whole, not loose teeth.

The Dark Lady's court thinks Beren's Peril is a wolf problem. I'd like to put a row of those on a table in front of somebody and have them count, and then explain to me again why this is a job for one packbreaker and a borrowed sergeant.
sps_peril_teeth.accept_text: Slip the strings off over the heads, whole. A cut string loses the order of the teeth.
sps_peril_teeth.turn_in_text:
She lays them out longest to shortest.

Look at the length of that one.

That isn't a wolf problem. That's a succession, and it's been running up there for years while the court has been filing us under vermin.

sps_pond_edge.description:
Right, here's what I actually think, and you're the first person I've said it to, because the March haven't the time and the Apothecaries would want it in writing.

The pond is draining, slowly, a hand's width a season, maybe, and it's been doing it since before the oozes started. I've got marks on three stones to prove it.

And here's the part I like less. The water's going somewhere, and something's coming the other way. Whatever rises in that pond isn't drowning in it, it's arriving.

Walk the whole edge for me. I don't mean my circuit. I mean the whole edge, the far side included, and tell me where the ground is wet that shouldn't be and dry that shouldn't be. Olivia's Pond is west of here, and the far bank is the west one.
sps_pond_edge.accept_text: Push a stick into the mud every few paces. You'll feel where it's soft that shouldn't be.
sps_pond_edge.turn_in_text:
He marks it on a board scratched with his own survey.

There, that's the low point, and that's where it's going, and that's nowhere near the stream.

So it isn't draining away, it's draining down. That means there's a space under that pond big enough to take two years of water.

sps_pond_ooze.description:
I'm Marshwalker Thorne. When you go out to Olivia's Pond, keep to the firm ground and follow the trodden path. It's trodden for a reason.

I've walked the edge of Olivia's Pond every day for two years. I know that water. I know where it's shallow, and I know which stones move.

For about three weeks now, something's been walking it with me: oozes out of the marsh, swamp ghouls, bloated things that were people. They aren't wandering in from elsewhere. They're coming up out of the pond itself, and they're doing it on my circuit.

I'd like fewer companions. And I'd like to stop checking behind me on a walk I could do with my eyes shut.
sps_pond_ooze.accept_text: Watch the water behind you, not in front. They come up where you've already walked.
sps_pond_ooze.turn_in_text:
I walked the whole circuit alone, and it took me the usual time, which it hasn't for a month.

That's much better. Now come back tomorrow, because that's the symptom, and I want to talk to you about the cause.

sps_pond_samples.description:
The bloated ones carry gas. You'll have noticed, if you've been close enough and regretted it.

It's in bladders, under the skin, and it isn't rot, because rot smells of rot and this doesn't. I've a strong suspicion it's what's coming up as the water goes down, collecting in whatever's nearest and hollow.

I want sealed samples, properly sealed, mind. If it's what I think it is, a sample in an open jar is a sample of air by the time you're back here.

If I'm right, the oozes and the ghouls aren't the problem. They're both just what happens to anything that sits in this gas long enough, and the remedy is at the source.
sps_pond_samples.turn_in_text:
He opens one a crack, sniffs, and shuts it fast.

That's the smell. That's what's in the air on the far side on a still morning.

I've been breathing that for two years, which explains a number of things about my last two years that I'd put down to the job.

sps_pyre_ambush.description:
I'm Hearthwarden Brand. Stand by the fire, not in the doorway. The doorway is where they look.

The worgen out there were the people of this village. I say that to everyone who comes through, and most of them nod and then go out and get surprised anyway, so I'll put it differently. They hunt like Pyrewood. They ambush from the treeline, the same way the men here always worked a deer, because the trick is the same trick and the knowing of it stayed.

The ambushers hold the treeline and the ferals come in behind. Thin them out. I'd rather not have to say this, but the dead are drifting this way too, and I can hold one of those problems or the other.
sps_pyre_ambush.accept_text: Walk the treeline slowly. They wait for you to hurry, the way a deer does.
sps_pyre_ambush.turn_in_text:
The treeline's quiet enough that I had the shutters open an hour.

I grew up here. I'd like to be able to look at my own trees without doing arithmetic about them.

sps_pyre_cultists.accept_text: Don't let them finish a chant. Brand says the ones they finish are the ones that answer.

sps_pyre_hall.description:
Pyrewood Hall is at the north end. You'll have seen the roofline from the lane.

Half the roof's gone. What's left of the doors is barred, and barred from the inside, which I've confirmed from the steps, and which is the detail that's kept me out of it for two years.

Something barred those doors. It was something that could work a bar, and wanted to be on the inside, and hasn't come out.

I'm not asking you to go in. I'm asking you to stand on the steps, properly, long enough to listen, and tell me what's behind them. Then I'll decide whether this village has a hall or a problem with a roof on it.
sps_pyre_hall.accept_text: Count the voices if you hear any. A number is more use to me than a feeling.
sps_pyre_hall.turn_in_text:
You heard a voice giving orders? There's nobody in that hall to give orders to, and there hasn't been since before the worgen. Either he's talking to the dead, or the dead are in there with him and listening.

I scraped a phial of ash off those steps the night the doors were barred, and I gave it to Avery Lusk by the fire. He'll want you to carry it south.

sps_pyre_sigils.accept_text: Wrap them in cloth before you carry them. Cut iron like that has edges.

sps_quillfire.description:
There's a colleague of mine in that tower, and I've run out of ways to avoid this conversation.

His name is Magister Quillfire, and he never left. When the plague came the rest of us went out the south road, and he stayed at his work, and he's been at his work ever since.

He casts at anyone who approaches now. That alone I could live with, because plenty of things in Silverpine cast at people.

What I can't live with is that the waygate answers him. When he works, it moves. He's a magister still conducting an experiment, not a ghost rattling about a tower, and he's the reason the thing you just described to me is open wider than it was.

I can't do it. I've tried twice to walk up that stair. Please, do it for me.
sps_quillfire.accept_text: Don't touch anything on his desk. It's all still part of the experiment.
sps_quillfire.turn_in_text:
The old magister doesn't ask how it went.

The gate has steadied. I could feel it even here, which I couldn't this morning.

He was better than me, and I'd like that said while there's somebody to say it to. He was better than me and he stayed, and I didn't, and both of those have been true for years, and I've only just put them in the same sentence.

sps_quilts.description:
Sit down a minute, you've been walking.

I'm Merriam Bucklebree. I sewed a quilt for every child born on this farm, mine, the hands', anyone's. Every one of them was different, and I can still tell you whose is whose by the backing.

The barn ghouls have dragged them off. They sleep on them. That's all they want them for. They've nested in the hay with my quilts under them, and I've watched them do it from the kitchen window.

I'd like the pieces back. I'm not daft, there'll be nothing whole left. But if I can get scraps I can piece them together into one, and then this family will be in a single blanket instead of a barn full of bedding for the dead.
sps_quilts.accept_text: Shake the hay out of them before you bring them in. I'd rather not have the barn in my kitchen.
sps_quilts.turn_in_text:
She lays them out on the table and sorts them without hesitating once.

That one's Tam. That's little Annie. That blue's my eldest, and this one here with the bad corner is the first I ever made, and it was always the worst.

I'll have them in one by winter. Thank you, love. Go and get something to eat.

sps_road_south.description:
Godfrey's dealt with, and that was the last of it. I've been going through what's left, and there isn't a reason to keep anybody here any more.

So I'll tell you what's south, since you won't have been.

The pines thin out past the pyre. And then there's a line, an actual line you can stand on, where the blight stops. I've stood with one boot either side of it. Behind you it's Silverpine, and in front of you the grass is green, and the road goes down from there into a valley that still grows things.

I haven't crossed it. I was born in Pyrewood, and I'll likely end in it.

So you go. Stand on the line, and then go down the road, and see what a valley looks like when it never got this.
sps_road_south.turn_in_text:
Brand asks you to describe it twice, and the second time he doesn't look at you.

It's green the whole way down, and there are people working in it.

Thank you. I'd got to where I couldn't quite believe that was still a thing that existed somewhere, and it means something to me to believe it, even from here.

sps_scout_report.description:
I'm Deathguard Lyle. You'll be going south, and I've got something that needs to go south, and those two facts are about to become the same fact.

This is for Sergeant Dallow at Valgan's Field. It's a report on the south road, what I've counted off this gate for the last few months, and it's short, and it isn't good.

I'd send a runner. The March has none to spare, and the Rear Guard won't lend me one for something I can't call urgent. I can't call it urgent, because the whole point of the report is that nothing has happened yet.

It's sealed, so keep it that way. I trust you. But if Dallow opens it himself he'll know nobody's had a chance to soften it, and a soft report is worth nothing to a man holding a field.
sps_scout_report.accept_text: If Dallow asks what I think, tell him I'd rather be wrong. He'll know what I mean.
sps_scout_report.turn_in_text:
Dallow reads it twice and sets it face down.

Lyle's counted the same thing I've counted, from the other end, without either of us saying it to the other.

That's what I needed. It isn't the numbers. It's that two men looking at opposite ends of the same road arrived somewhere unpleasant independently.

sps_sfk_forecourt.description:
I want to ask you something, and I want an honest answer rather than a kind one.

I've stood at that gate for years. The howling comes down out of that keep every night, and it's never once stopped.

And I can't tell you any more whether it's got louder, or whether I've simply got used to it and lost my measure. Those are very different facts, and I've no way to tell them apart from the gate, because the only instrument I had was me, and I've been standing in it too long.

Go and stand in the forecourt. Don't go inside, just the forecourt. Listen to it with ears that haven't heard it before, and then come back and tell me straight. The forecourt of Shadowfang Keep is a long way south of here.
sps_sfk_forecourt.accept_text: Stay in the forecourt longer than you'd like. The first minute won't tell you anything.
sps_sfk_forecourt.turn_in_text:
Marl takes that without flinching.

So it's louder.

Then it isn't me. I'd half hoped it was me. A man going strange at his post is a smaller problem than a keep getting worse.

I'll send that up tonight and they'll do nothing with it, and I'll have said it.

sps_sfk_pickets.description:
Marl has the days on the Shadowfang gate and I've got the nights, and the road past the pickets is the worst of both. The ghouls and the stalkers crowd it, and they aren't coming down it. They're pressed up against it, facing the keep, as if something inside were calling them.

There's a party going in soon, and I'd rather they spent what they've got inside instead of on the way up.

Clear the Rotting Ghouls and the Feral Worgen Stalkers off the keep road. The keep road runs south past Beren's Peril.
sps_sfk_pickets.accept_text: Leave a path clear down the middle of the road. The party will need it.

sps_shut_gate.description:
I want you to go and look at the gate itself, properly, up close, and I'll tell you why in a moment.

That gate hasn't opened since the night Gilneas shut itself off. There hasn't been a crack, or a hinge-shift, nothing, and I've got the detail's log going back to before I took it, and every corporal has written the same word in it every night.

Here's my trouble. I've been writing that word for eleven months, and about a month ago I realised I'd stopped actually looking before I wrote it. You get into the habit of a thing being true.

So go and look, and come back and tell me what you see rather than what the log says. If it's still shut, I'd like to have been told so by somebody who checked. The Greymane Wall gate is south-east of here.
sps_shut_gate.accept_text: Put your hand on the gate if you can reach it. Tell me if it's warm or cold.
sps_shut_gate.turn_in_text:
So it's still shut.

He writes it in the log, and says he'll go and look himself before he signs it.

Now it's true because it's true, and not because it's always been true. That's worth the walk.

sps_talon_stalkers.description:
I'm Trapper Hask. When you go up my hill, don't climb the scree, go round it. That slope moves, and it'll take you down into the stalkers, which is where they prefer their meals delivered.

It's called Berard's Talon, broken stone the whole ridge, above the old keep road.

The crag stalkers work the slopes and the wraiths drift the crest, and between the two of them I haven't set a line on that hill in a year and a half. A trapper who can't set lines is a man standing on a hill with opinions.

Clear the slopes and the crest. Then I can work, and when I'm working I notice things, and that hill has a great deal worth noticing on it.
sps_talon_stalkers.accept_text: Look up as often as you look ahead. The wraiths drift down from the crest without a sound.
sps_talon_stalkers.turn_in_text: I set a run of lines this afternoon. And you're right about the crest. You can see the whole keep road from up there. I'd forgotten that was the reason anybody ever cared about that hill.

sps_talon_tokens.description:
Here's the thing I noticed, now I can get up there.

The wraiths carry tokens, little things, a coin, a button, a ring, held in the fingers. Every one of them has got one, and not one of them has got two.

A scavenger would have a pocketful. This is each of them holding the one thing, and I've a strong feeling it's the one thing they were buried with, and somebody has taken them out of those graves.

Get the tokens for me. I know the plots along the keep road. There's a burying ground at the bottom of that hill that nobody's tended since Berard's day.

I'd like to put them back. A trapper's got time in the winter, and I haven't had anything worth doing with it.
sps_talon_tokens.turn_in_text:
He turns a button over.

That's Gilnean work, and the coin's older than the keep.

I'll start at the bottom plots and work up. It'll take me the winter, and I've got the winter.

sps_wall_breakers.description:
I'm Corporal Teague, of the Greymane Wall detail. I'm down at the March for supplies, and I'll tell you up front that my posting makes no sense and I'm doing it anyway.

The worgen come at that wall every night. They throw themselves at a sealed gate in a wall that nothing has come through in years, and they do it until they can't, and then the next night they do it again.

And the dead of the Wall Guard rise to meet them, the Gilneans. They form up on their side, in their own kit, and hold a gate nobody is defending against an enemy that can't get through it.

Thin the breakers. Calm the ghosts if there's a way, and I don't believe there is. Both sides of that wall have been fighting a war that ended, and I'd settle for one quiet night.
sps_wall_breakers.accept_text: Go to the Greymane Wall, a long way south. The breakers are on our side, and the Guard's ghosts on theirs.
sps_wall_breakers.turn_in_text:
It's quiet, with nothing at the gate at all.

He listens for a while.

I've been on this detail eleven months, and I've never heard that wall be silent. I don't like it half as much as I expected to.

sps_wall_seals.description:
There's something the Wall Guard carry, and I'd like it off them before anybody else thinks of it.

They carry the seals they swore their oaths on. Every Gilnean guardsman had one, and they went into the wall with them, and they're still holding them.

The Forsaken relief comes down the Wall road next month. Somebody in that column is going to look at a row of ghosts holding Gilnean seals and see salvage, and I'd very much like the seals to be somewhere else by then.

I'm going to lay them on the shut gate, all of them, on the step, where they'd have been laid if there'd been anybody left to do it properly. Then whatever the relief does, that part will already have been done right. The Greymane Wall is south of here.
sps_wall_seals.accept_text: Take them gently. Those men held those seals a long time.
sps_wall_seals.turn_in_text:
Teague sets them out along the gate step one at a time, in no order you can see.

That's that done.

I'm Forsaken, a corporal in an army that'd take that wall tomorrow if it could. And I've just laid out a dead enemy's oaths on his own doorstep, and I'd do it again, and I'd thank you not to put that in anything written.

sps_wall_warden.description:
There's one on the parapet, and he's the reason none of this ends.

He's the Wall's last commander. He's still enforcing the order he was given on the night it went up, and the order was nothing in, nothing out.

He isn't holding it against the worgen, and he isn't holding it against us. He's holding it against everything, which is what the order said, and he's been holding it for years against a country that hasn't sent anybody out to be stopped.

And before you ask, yes, I've tried the obvious. The Forsaken can't pass him either. I've watched our own people turned back off that parapet by a dead Gilnean doing his job.

He was given a sentence and nobody ever lifted it. So we lift it.
sps_wall_warden.turn_in_text:
Teague looks up at the empty parapet.

That's the sentence served, then.

I'll put it in the log as the detail is complete, which is the only honest thing I've written on this posting.

sps_wight_bones.description:
I'm Field Surgeon Ashe. Hold still a moment. No, you're fine, I was checking the shoulder. It's a habit.

I've run out of bone. Say that to a living surgeon and they'll look at you strangely. Say it to me and you'll understand immediately why it's a crisis. Half the March is held together with replacements, and the other half is about to need some.

The battlefield wights out on Valgan's Field are wearing the bones of better men than any of us. They're Third War dead, mostly, good stock, properly grown, with no rickets in them.

I'm not too proud to recycle, and neither is anyone who's had a femur out of me. Bring me what you can, and I'll be glad of it.
sps_wight_bones.accept_text: Bring the femurs if you can. I'm short of everything, but I'm shortest of those.
sps_wight_bones.turn_in_text:
She sorts them by length without looking up.

These are excellent. Somebody fed these men properly once.

I'll have three of the March back on their feet by the week's end. Don't tell them where it came from. Some of them still have opinions about that, which I find remarkable given where the rest of them came from.
